```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
lets = c("A","B","C")
turns = c("-","+")
chars = c(lets,turns)

while(T){
  nls = sample(3:5,3)
  s1 = sample(chars,nls[1],T)
  s2 = sample(chars,nls[2],T)
  s3 = sample(chars,nls[3],T)
  if(length(unique(s1))>1 && length(unique(s2))>1 && length(unique(s3))>1){break}
}

s1 = paste0(c(sample(lets,1),s1),collapse="")
s2 = paste0(c(sample(lets,1),s2),collapse="")
s3 = paste0(c(sample(lets,1),s3),collapse="")

for(i in 1:10){
  s1 = gsub("+-","++",s1,fixed=T)
  s2 = gsub("+-","++",s2,fixed=T)
  s3 = gsub("+-","++",s3,fixed=T)
  s1 = gsub("-+","--",s1,fixed=T)
  s2 = gsub("-+","--",s2,fixed=T)
  s3 = gsub("-+","--",s3,fixed=T)
}

s1 = unlist(strsplit(s1, split = ""))
s2 = unlist(strsplit(s2, split = ""))
s3 = unlist(strsplit(s3, split = ""))

if(sample(c(T,F),1)){
  s1 = c(s1,sample(lets,1),rev(s1))
} else {
  s1 = c(s1,rev(s1))
}
if(sample(c(T,F),1)){
  s2 = c(s2,sample(lets,1),rev(s2))
} else {
  s2 = c(s2,rev(s2))
}
if(sample(c(T,F),1)){
  s3 = c(s3,sample(lets,1),rev(s3))
} else {
  s3 = c(s3,rev(s3))
}

whichbads = sample(1:3,2,T)

if(1 %in% whichbads){
  n = sample(1:length(s1),1)
  s1[n] = sample(chars,1)
}
if(2 %in% whichbads){
  n = sample(1:length(s2),1)
  s2[n] = sample(chars,1)
}
if(3 %in% whichbads){
  n = sample(1:length(s3),1)
  s3[n] = sample(chars,1)
}

s1l = s1
s2l = s2
s3l = s3

s1 = paste0(s1,collapse="")
s2 = paste0(s2,collapse="")
s3 = paste0(s3,collapse="")

if(paste0(s1l,collapse="") == paste0(rev(s1l),collapse="")){
  sol1 = "10"
} else {
  sol1 = "01"
}

if(paste0(s2l,collapse="") == paste0(rev(s2l),collapse="")){
  sol2 = "10"
} else {
  sol2 = "01"
}

if(paste0(s3l,collapse="") == paste0(rev(s3l),collapse="")){
  sol3 = "10"
} else {
  sol3 = "01"
}


```

Question
========

When all replacement strings are **[palindromes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palindrome)**, the resulting [L-system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L-system) pattern will have mirror symmetry, which helps create more compelling image. In nature, most animals (including humans) display [bilateral symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetry_in_biology#Bilateral_symmetry).

Consider the replacement rules below.

`A > `r s1`` \
`B > `r s2`` \
`C > `r s3``

For each replacement rule, is the replacement palindromic?

* Does `A > `r s1`` have a palindromic replacement?

##ANSWER1##

* Does `B > `r s2`` have a palindromic replacement?

##ANSWER2##

* Does `C > `r s3`` have a palindromic replacement?

##ANSWER3##

Answerlist
--------

* Yes
* No
* Yes
* No
* Yes
* No
